queries.text: "para nos tomarem por aí" is unusual; read as "to take us for a ride" (to exploit/fool us). Alternatives: "to take hold of us," "to get the better of us."
"revolta" rendered "resentment" to keep it distinct from "rebeldia" ("rebelliousness") in 22-0034, which the author sets on the other side. Alternatives: "revolt," "outrage."
Heading "Irritação da dúvida" rendered "The irritation of doubt," the phrase used in Charles S. Peirce’s "The Fixation of Belief" (1877, public domain), which the author points to here.
"o uso de relatos e perguntas" read as relying on women’s own accounts and on asking them questions; rendered "accounts and questionnaires." Alternative: "accounts and questions."
"desencarnação" (spiritist term for death, the soul leaving the body) rendered "discarnation." Alternative: "hastens death."
